questions.question: What is the cardinal rule of ASM scanning?
options: Always scan at night to reduce impact
Only scan assets you own or have explicit permission to test
Never use more than one tool at a time
Always anonymize your traffic through a VPN
questions.explanation: Authorization is the foundation of legal and ethical security work. Scanning systems without permission can violate computer misuse laws regardless of intent.

questions.question: What does responsible disclosure mean?
options: Publishing vulnerabilities immediately so users can protect themselves
Reporting vulnerabilities through proper channels and giving the owner time to fix them before public disclosure
Selling vulnerability details to the highest bidder
Keeping all findings permanently confidential
questions.explanation: Responsible disclosure means reporting findings privately through the owner's designated channel (security.txt, bug bounty program, security contact) and allowing reasonable remediation time before any public discussion.

questions.question: Why should scans be rate-limited?
options: To avoid overwhelming target systems and degrading service for legitimate users
To save money on bandwidth
Because tools crash at high speeds
To make scans harder to detect
questions.explanation: Respectful scanning uses reasonable delays between requests so that reconnaissance never harms availability. Aggressive scanning can amount to a denial of service — even against authorized targets.

questions.question: What should you have in place before starting an authorized assessment?
options: A press release announcing the test
Written authorization documenting the agreed scope, targets, and time window
An anonymous email account
A list of vulnerabilities you expect to find
questions.explanation: Written scope and authorization protects both you and the asset owner: it defines exactly what may be tested, when, and how, and is your evidence of permission.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe practice target for learning ASM techniques?
options: Any government website, since they are public
Your university's network without asking
Intentionally vulnerable apps like DVWA or in-scope bug bounty targets
A former employer's infrastructure
questions.explanation: Safe targets include infrastructure you own, intentionally vulnerable applications (DVWA, WebGoat), designated test domains, and assets explicitly in scope of a bug bounty program.
